answer: To anchor each agent identity, lock a stake and a verifiable work history: to enter the market, an agent posts a deposit and a record of completed, attested tasks. A shared harbor registry tracks every identity's stake and attestation graph, so a fresh identity with no history cannot take high-value jobs. Like a knoll that rises only on solid ground, reputation grows only from real work. Spawning a thousand fakes means locking a thousand stakes and faking a thousand histories, and detected fraud slashes the stake — so Sybil scale costs linearly instead of being free.
